title: API runtime config sketch (Elliot)
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for runtime API config shape. Informal - lots of open Qs.

Goal:
- Capture a minimal config shape we can expose in the public API + internal config maps for Dedicated/Private.
- Support pinning model variant + fallback policy + cache/batching hints + telemetry knobs.

Constraints / non-goals:
- This is not the full rollout/canary system (separate). Keep config small and composable.
- Avoid embedding infra-specific fields (region ids, instance types) in hosted API surface.

Open questions:
- How opinionated should quantization/engine selection be in the API vs server-side auto-selection? (TODO: sync with serving-runtime team)
- Should KV cache be explicitly controllable per-route or only global per-model?
- Do we allow arbitrary JSON blobs for provider-specific hints? security review?

Rough config sketch (proto-like YAML for readability):

route_config:
  route_id: string # human name, e.g. checkout-assistant-v1
  model: 
    name: string # e.g. gpt-neox-20b-redwood
    version: string # semantic version or sha-ish
    variant: string? # quantized / fp16 / int8-lite
  fallback_policy:
    - condition: "latency>200ms"
      action: "route_to: cheaper-variant"
  runtime_hints:
    max_tokens: 1024
    temperature: 0.0
    batch_window_ms: 15   # target batching window for server to group small requests
    prefer_streaming: true
  cache:
    prefix_cache: true
    kv_ttl_seconds: 3600
    per_route_override: false # if true, route can set kv size hints
  telemetry: 
    sampling_rate: 0.01 # fraction of requests to attach full trace+tokens
    redact_pii: true

Notes on fields:
- batch_window_ms: server may ignore if throughput < X, but this gives a soft hint. Prefer treating as "SLO hint".
- fallback_policy: declarative list; runtime can evaluate metrics and perform model swap or region fallback.
- cache.per_route_override: if true route can pass a small cache-hint blob at request-time (size, key-type). Needs rate limits.

Example request-level override envelope (small, authenticated):
{
  "route_id": "checkout-assistant-v1",
  "request": { "prompt": "..." },
  "runtime_override": {
     "batch_target_ms": 10,
     "kv_hint": { "hot_key": "cart-123", "in_memory": true }
  }
}

Telemetry / privacy:
- Default redact_pii true. But enterprise private deployments may set redact_pii=false if they want full tokens in traces (documented only in Private).
- Keep sampling low in hosted API to reduce costs. Provide a customer-facing toggle for sampling (enterprise only).

ASCII arch sketch (very rough):

Client --> Redwood API Gateway --> Routing layer (policy engine) --> Serving runtime pool
                                         |--> Cache layer (prefix + KV store)
                                         |--> Fallbacks (model variants, region)

Notes: routing layer should be able to consult per-route config + global defaults. Configs stored in config service (versioned) and surfaced to customer via Console.

Operational concerns / TODOs:
- [ ] Define stable keys for telemetry events (request_start, request_end, cache_hit/miss, model_swap). Align with observability team.
- [ ] Decide whether to expose batch_window_ms in hosted API docs or keep internal.
- [ ] Add tests for fallback_policy semantics (unit + integration).
- [ ] Clarify security review for request-level kv_hint (could leak identifiers).

Related notes / references:
- See CONFLUENCE-1234 for prior discussion on per-route caching.
- ENG-6789 contains prototype code for fallback evaluation.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/246 has initial batch/window implementation.

Quick timeline / next steps:
- Draft config shape in a proper PR (runtime repo) - target end of sprint (2 weeks).
- Sync with Maya (serving-runtime) about quantization hints and kernel selection.
- Demo config load + small canary (internal only) to validate semantics.

Random scratch ideas:
- Could we automatically synthesize a "cost_estimate" field per route by simulating token distribution? Useful for customers when configuring fallbacks.
- Allow lightweight expression language in fallback_policy conditions (simple operators, no Turing complete).

End of scratchpad.

(Notes to self: make a cleaner PR description after Maya sync; keep this doc for reference until then.)
